newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Steady to down despite firm crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Steady to down despite firm crude.

text.p: A recovery in crude prices failed to provide support to the bearish prompt gas oil market which has been on a downtrend for most of this week, traders said on Friday.
Crude values on London's International Petroleum Exchange gained 14 cents to be last quoted at $18.46 per barrel for July.
A rise in IPE gas oil futures in London by $1.00 per tonne to $166.75 helped to boost swaps values but failed to do likewise for the physical market.
"The problem is, nobody wants to take the oil right now as China is closed," one traders said.

This lack of interest is seen on the physical market as only two bids were seen for late June/early July liftings at low levels of $24.30 and $24.50 per barrel free-on-board basis, with offers seen at $24.80-$24.90. No deals were seen.
Most offers were seen for prompt cargoes at lower levels of between $24.25 and $24.40 per barrel, but faced no takers.
The six sellers were dominated by refiners and producers and only one trader, indicating the supply glut in regional refineries.

Traders said refiners have been moving gas oil to Hong Kong for storage with deals seen recently at 70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight basis. This was much lower than deals seen a month ago at around $1.00-premiums. Swaps gas oil for June recovered from its 20-cents fall earlier in the day to be quoted late in the day at $24.50/$24.60, up five cents from Thursday.
Jet fuel was not doing any better either with the jet/gas oil regrade widening to -50/-40 cents from Thursday's -30/-10 cents.
